title: The problem map: a problem as parts, sub-problems and an ordered composition, drawn by rules and judged by one validator
request: Phase 2 of the owner's plan: an agentic system that understands a problem, breaks a complex one into parts and sub-problems with a big-picture workflow, and composes their solutions; and the rule that every package is adoptable by the main product.
spec: dclab_core.problem_map (ProblemMap v1, decompose, validate, fingerprint), adapters.main_product_problem_map.problem_specs, the conformance entry, the schema and its baseline, CHANGELOG 0.50.0, a CORE_INTEGRATION section.
plan: A contract that a person, a rule and later a model can all fill, and one validator that judges all of them the same way.
Templates only where the words say the shape; anything else stays one problem, so no single problem is split by accident.
A map the main product can hold: one ProblemSpec proposal per sub-problem, the places in the map in a free-form key, the composition once.

decisions.decision: The constructor checks shape; validate returns every issue in words.
decisions.why: A person's edit can be shown all its reasons at once, and a model's map is judged by the same function as the rules' map.

decisions.decision: A missing unit or moment is a question for the reviewer (24.2), not an unsound map.
decisions.why: The words often do not say; refusing the map would force a guess, and a guessed moment is where leakage starts.

decisions.decision: Ranks order the moments: an outcome must be known strictly before a reader's rank, and after its own prediction.
decisions.why: One integer per sub-problem is enough to name the leak a late verdict would cause, and to say which read is allowed.

decisions.decision: A composition is built in order from sub-problems and earlier outputs, with the key where two units meet, and leaves out no sub-problem nobody reads.
decisions.why: The composer of 24.5 must be able to run it step by step; a result that is left out is a part of the problem silently dropped.

decisions.decision: The fingerprint is the structure (units, moments, families, labels, ranks, needs, reads with keys, steps in order, budget), not the wording.
decisions.why: Ledger points and the adapter key on it; two maps that validate differently must not share one.

change: dclab_core problem_map.py (new), adapters/main_product_problem_map.py (new), adapters/conformance.py, contracts.py, schemas/problem_map.json and its baseline, CHANGELOG 0.50.0 and the version, scripts/core_wheel_check.py, docs (CORE_INTEGRATION, the plan), tests/test_problem_map.py (74 tests), tests/test_conformance.py.

findings.defect: The budget pattern missed the way people say it.
findings.scenario: 'the team can review 200 a day' gave no budget, so the review step had none.
findings.cause: The pattern knew 'reviewers can check N' only.
findings.fix: Reviewer, team, we and they, check, review, handle and investigate, a count or 'a few', and 'N cases a day' are read; the phrase is clipped.

findings.defect: The fraud template said 'ride' for every unit.
findings.scenario: 'Find fraudulent insurance claims' got parts about rides, couriers and bikers.
findings.cause: The template was written from one example.
findings.fix: The unit is the first thing the words name (ride, order, delivery, claim, account), else the actor; titles, tables and the key follow it.

findings.defect: An outcome known at the reader's own moment passed the leak rule.
findings.scenario: A test set the outcome earlier than its own prediction.
findings.cause: The rule compared with greater-than only.
findings.fix: An outcome must be known strictly before the reader's rank, and after its own prediction.

findings.defect: The composition checks were far weaker than their message.
findings.scenario: A budget step before the fusion that makes its input, a step feeding on its own output, two steps feeding each other, an output equal to a sub-problem id, duplicate outputs, a step with no inputs and a composition naming only sp1 all returned no issue.
findings.cause: Any step's output was accepted as an input.
findings.fix: The steps are walked in order: an input is a sub-problem or an earlier output, an output is a new name, a step has inputs, and a sub-problem nobody reads must feed a step.

findings.defect: A map changed after it was made kept its fingerprint through validate and the adapter.
findings.scenario: model_copy changed sp1's family to regression: validate gave no issue and the specs carried the old fingerprint, which ledger points would key on.
findings.cause: model_copy skips the validators and validate never compared the fingerprint; the fingerprint was not among the fields set, so a dump without defaults dropped it.
findings.fix: validate names a stale fingerprint, the adapter refuses it, and the fingerprint is a set field.

findings.defect: The fingerprint left out structure that validate depends on.
findings.scenario: Dropping a read's key kept the fingerprint and turned a sound map into an unsound one; a different budget or a reordered sequence gave the same one.
findings.cause: It hashed ids, families and sorted reads only.
findings.fix: It covers units, moments, labels, ranks, needs, reads with their keys, the steps in order with their keys, and the budget.

findings.defect: The templates split sentences that only shared words with them.
findings.scenario: A priority question 'before it is routed' became a team and urgency sequence; 'abusive comments in orders' and a fully labelled 'is_fraud' column got the fraud template; a discount question about orders was forced to forecasting.
findings.cause: Single words were enough, and the card's family was overridden.
findings.fix: A routing needs a team, a connector and an urgency in that order; 'abuse' is not fraud; a stated label column is one problem; a template needs the card not to say another family; a forecast template needs the card to say forecasting.

findings.defect: A denial of confirmed cases became labels 'file'.
findings.scenario: 'None of them were confirmed', 'We have not confirmed any yet' and 'There are no known cases' all kept a classifier on a file of known cases.
findings.cause: The words 'confirmed' and 'known' matched whatever came with them.
findings.fix: A clause that mentions confirmed cases with a negation denies them; a clause without one says they exist; nothing said is unknown; a denial drops the classifier.

findings.defect: decompose raised on three kinds of input.
findings.scenario: A budget phrase with a 700-digit number, a brief of 13 parts, and a part that is not a record each raised.
findings.cause: Text was not clipped to the contract's limits; a step allowed 12 inputs; parts were assumed to be dictionaries.
findings.fix: The budget phrase is clipped, a step takes as many inputs as there are sub-problems, a brief is cut at 20 parts with a note, and what is not a part is skipped.

findings.defect: The unit rule compared only the unit a sub-problem set itself, and a fusion across units had no key.
findings.scenario: A sub-problem with no unit under an account part could read a ride sub-problem with no key; the leak was reported only after the key was added; the fraud template's own fusion mixed rides and accounts with nowhere to say how they join.
findings.cause: An elif chain, and the key existed only on reads.
findings.fix: The effective unit is the sub-problem's own, else its part's; both issues are reported; a step has a joins key and the joined result is on the first input's unit.

findings.defect: Rank holes: an outcome known when it is predicted, and an outcome of a sub-problem with no label.
findings.scenario: known_rank equal to predict_rank passed; a sub-problem with labels none could have a known outcome that another read.
findings.cause: The check was a strict less-than and labels were not compared with ranks.
findings.fix: known_rank no later than predict_rank is refused, as is a known rank on a sub-problem that says no label exists.

findings.defect: The adapter had a dead size branch, dropped multiclass, could produce an empty objective, and a test could not fail.
findings.scenario: constraints never exceed the limit; kind multiclass became classification; a blank title gave an empty business_objective; a test asserted the word 'rows' is absent.
findings.cause: Written before the contract's limits were fixed.
findings.fix: The branch is replaced by a test of the largest place; multiclass is kept; titles are stripped and non-blank and the objective falls back to the id; a test checks that no string or list in the contract is unbounded, so a table cannot be stored in a map.

measurements.name: dev journeys split by the rules
measurements.gate: At most 0 of the 15 single-problem sentences of the dev journeys are split into parts (written before the templates).
measurements.result: 0 of 15 sentences split; every map validates.
limits: Only single-problem sentences: it shows no false split, not that every complex problem is found. The sealed set is read once, at the end of the phase.
measurements.against_gate: 0 split against a limit of 0 of 15: met.

outcome: A person's words become a validated map; the fraud problem is four parts (three when no case was confirmed) with the right families, a churn question is one; a leak, a missing key, a cycle and a composition that cannot run are each refused with their reason; the main product holds the map as one spec proposal per sub-problem.
lessons: A template that fires on words alone splits problems that only share them: require the shape, and let the card's own reading veto it.
A hash used as an identity must cover everything the validator reads, and the validator must check the hash, or an edited copy keeps the old name.
Test a negation: 'confirmed' in a sentence says nothing about whether any case was.
Walk a composition in order: a set of names hides the step that uses a result before it is made.
risks: The templates cover a fraud problem and a two-step routing; the model decomposer (24.2) reads the rest, and is switched on only after a sealed measurement against these rules.
Whether the main product's parse_objective keeps the free-form key was not readable at the pinned commit.
